quotes.text: Normal search helps you find your own work. It's built for day-to-day tasks, like locating a document from last week or finding an email from a customer.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why everyday search is not enough for an investigation.

quotes.text: A legal hold is a preservation rule. It keeps relevant content available while a case remains active, even if someone later tries to delete or change that content.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a clear, compact definition of a legal hold.

quotes.text: Retention asks, how long should we normally keep this kind of work? A legal hold asks, could this content matter in this case right now?
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Neatly contrasts retention and legal hold, a common source of confusion.

quotes.text: If you close a case, the holds connected to that case can be released, so closing a case is not just housekeeping.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Highlights an easily overlooked consequence of closing an eDiscovery case.

quotes.text: Many people think the safest move is searching the whole organization first, but it usually isn't.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Challenges the instinct to run overly broad searches.

takeaways: eDiscovery is a case-based process: define the matter, pick data sources, apply holds, search, review and only then export.
Know where Microsoft 365 stores work, for example Teams chats in Exchange Online mailboxes and chat files in OneDrive, so searches stay focused and complete.
Prepare before a crisis by building a data map, tightening eDiscovery permissions, agreeing on case naming and escalation paths, and checking licensing for premium review.
hook: When a complaint, regulator request or data exposure hits, panicked manual digging through inboxes destroys context and evidence. This episode walks IT, legal, HR and compliance teams through Microsoft Purview eDiscovery in plain English. You will learn how cases, legal holds, searches, review sets and exports form one defensible process.
